newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP approves directive on cross-border payments.
newsitem.headline: EP approves directive on cross-border payments.

text.p: The European Parliament approved on Thursday new legislation designed to make cross-border payments within the European Union safer, quicker and cheaper.
The new directive on cross-border credit transfers, COM(96)172, will apply to payments of up to 50,000 Ecus, double the amount agreed by EU finance ministers in December 1995.
This follows pressure from the parliament, which sought to give greater protection to individuals and small businesses transferring money from one EU member state to another.
But under a compromise with the Council of Ministers, Euro-MPs accepted banks should not be obliged to refund more than 12,500 Ecus if a transfer failed to reach its destination.

The directive was introduced because of the banking industry's apparent inability to agree voluntary rules to improve cross-border transfers, which the European Commission and consumer groups say are lengthy, expensive and unreliable.
A 1993 Commission study showed that in many cases beneficiaries did not get the full amount sent to them because banks charged both the sender and the recipient for the service.
Banks are also criticised for not accepting responsibility for lost transfers.

The directive, which is not expected to come into force in all the member states for another two and a half years, obliges banks to complete payment transfers within five working days and bans double charging.
